meta.title: Legacy Campaigns
meta.description: The run's legacy campaign modes — seven challenge runs unlocked with hidden Easy Chat phrases, each with its own twist (weakest-Pokémon runs, one-hit trainer battles, auto-battle and more) and a low-is-better score tracked on your pause screen. They predate the modern quest-driven progression and live on in the hub's Config Room; the mechanics are identical between Vanilla and EX apart from the generation cap of the BST Cup and an EX-only mega-evolution score hook that no code path currently calls.

prose.heading: Challenge runs, the old way
prose.text: Campaigns are self-contained challenge modes for a run: one twist, one goal, one score. Unlike the modern quests, they are unlocked the old-school way — by saying a hidden two-word phrase to the assistant in your Config Room. Say the right thing and the campaign unlocks, and the next run you start plays under its rules. Seven phrases, seven campaigns; none of them combine with each other, and most work in any adventure type.

prose.heading: Scores and best runs
prose.text: Five of the seven campaigns are scored, and in every case lower is better. Four count how many of your Pokémon faint over the whole run; the BST Cup instead scores the highest Base Stat Total among everything you've carried. Your live score shows in the pause screen (the status menu grows a score line while a campaign is active), and if you finish a campaign run past the final boss, your best score is saved and shown next to the campaign when you talk to the assistant again. Completing a campaign run also marks it as done for your hall of fame.

records.name: Unlocking a campaign (hidden phrase)
records.description: The assistant in the hub's Config Room opens an Easy Chat screen titled 'What to say?'. If the phrase you type matches one of the hidden two-word campaign phrases, that campaign unlocks and becomes the desired campaign for your next run. The known phrases: 'SMALL HOLIDAY' (BST Cup), 'REFLECT ADVENTURE' (Classic), 'BATTLETOWER NOW' (Battle Addict), 'ATTACK WHAT' (Auto Battler), 'LATER MAN' (LaterManner), 'BALL OUT' (Limited Capture) and 'PLEASE MISS' (One Hit Mode). Once unlocked, the assistant offers the campaign by name with your best score.

records.name: How a campaign activates
records.description: When a run starts with an unlocked desired campaign, it is activated (unless you started the run by skipping straight to a difficulty, which disables campaigns) — but no announcement is ever shown: the 'Campaign Active!' and 'Aim for Low Score!' popup strings exist in the code, yet no code path ever pushes them, so the announcement the Config Room dialogue promises ('it'll be announced to you at the start of the Adventure') was never implemented. The BST Cup is the exception to 'works anywhere': it is cancelled if the run is in Gauntlet mode. Finishing the run at or past the final boss records your best score and marks the campaign complete.
records.source: src/rogue_campaign.c @vanilla L121-173 (activation: skip-to-difficulty disables, Gauntlet cancels BST Cup, per-campaign setup), L226-241 (completion at difficulty ≥ 14, best score saved) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_popup.c @vanilla L328, L330 ('Campaign Active!' / 'Aim for Low Score!' strings — defined but never pushed, no call sites) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: BST Cup (Low BST)
records.description: Finish a full run with the weakest Pokémon you can: your score is the highest Base Stat Total of any species you've ever carried in your party. The total is rechecked at the start of every battle and when a Pokémon changes form, but it is a ratchet that only ever moves up — catching a stronger Pokémon raises your score permanently, and releasing it does nothing (the Config Room's note that you can 'catch and release' to lower the score is wishful thinking). The run forces a fresh start — your config resets (Pokédex limited to generations 1–3 in Vanilla, 1–8 in EX), your party is wiped to a single level 15 Sunkern, you start with an Everstone Curse and a Species Clause Curse, 50 Link Cables and 8 Rare Candies, and TM06 (Toxic) is banned. Standard (Classic-style) adventures only — Gauntlet is not allowed.

differences.vanilla: The forced Pokédex generation cap is Gen 1–3.
differences.ex: The forced Pokédex generation cap is Gen 1–8 deliberately leaving Gen 9 species out of the pool. EX also carries an unused mega-evolution recheck for the tracked total (no code path calls it), which would let a Mega Evolution raise the score.

records.name: Classic Mode
records.description: A legacy campaign that unlocks but has no active rules in the run code today: it carries a title, an unlock phrase and a Config Room description, but no campaign check anywhere in the run behaves differently while it is active. It exists so the phrase still unlocks cleanly.

records.name: Battle Addict (Miniboss Battler)
records.description: The trainer-fight campaign: the Config Room description promises a run with no route encounters, only Strong Trainer (miniboss) battles, and your score is the number of your Pokémon that faint over the run — lower is better. The faint-count scoring is live; the 'no routes, only minibosses' path change is part of the legacy behaviour set (the path generator no longer special-cases this campaign), so in practice you get the score challenge on an otherwise normal path.

records.name: Auto Battler
records.description: Both you and your opponents pick moves at random in every battle — the same auto-move behaviour as the Auto Move Curse, applied for the whole run. Score is the faint count of your party over the run; lower is better. Works in any adventure type.
records.source: src/battle_controller_player.c @vanilla L3024-3026 (player moves auto-selected while the campaign is active), src/rogue_baked.c @vanilla L941, L955 (auto-pick in baked battle flows) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_campaign.c @vanilla L290-305 (faint-count scoring) (identical @origin/expansion); data/maps/Rogue_Hub_Interior_ConfigRoom/scripts.pory @vanilla L146-147 / @origin/expansion L146-147 (in-game description)

records.name: LaterManner Mode
records.description: A campaign 'made for the streamer himself': the run forces a fresh start with a single level 15 Farfetch'd, wild encounters are allowed to repeat species back-to-back (the usual anti-repeat filter is disabled), and your score is the faint count of your party — lower is better. The in-game description is deliberately vague: 'You'll figure out the rest.'
records.source: src/rogue_campaign.c @vanilla L121-173 (pre-activation: config reset), L200-212 (post-activation: Farfetch'd Lv15) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L8345-8352 / @origin/expansion L8336-8343 (anti-repeat wild-encounter filter disabled while active); data/maps/Rogue_Hub_Interior_ConfigRoom/scripts.pory @vanilla L150-152 / @origin/expansion L150-152 (in-game description)

records.name: Limited Capture (Pokeball Limit)
records.description: The no-catching challenge: every ball in your bag is banned for the run (all ball items, from Poké Balls up), and on activation five Poké Balls are removed and five Ultra Balls added for flavour. The goal is simply to complete the adventure without catching anything — Pokémon that are simply given to you (like the Lab's take-back) can still arrive. Unscored — it's about finishing, not scoring. Works in any adventure type.

records.name: One Hit Mode (One HP)
records.description: Every hit a trainer's Pokémon lands on your party faints you — in Trainer Battles, damage against your side is overridden to far exceed your max HP. Wild battles play normally, and damage-over-time and status effects work as usual, so the challenge is managing PP, status and which mon faces which trainer. Score is the faint count of your party over the run; lower is better. Works in any adventure type.

records.name: Campaign scores
records.description: Five campaigns are scored — BST Cup, Battle Addict, Auto Battler, LaterManner and One Hit — and in all of them lower is better. While a scored campaign is active, the run's status screen grows a score line. Best scores are saved when the run completes at or past the final boss, and are shown next to the campaign name in the Config Room and on the hall of fame.
